metadata.content: V8 engines returning to Formula 1 in 2030 as FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem describes move to 'reconnect with DNA' of the sport | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content V8 engines returning to Formula 1 in 2030 as FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem describes move to 'reconnect with DNA' of the sport Multiple Formula 1 drivers had backed for V8 engines to return to the sport; FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has confirmed V8 engines will return from 2030 after a 17-year absence; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Friday 20 November 2026 20:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Formula 1 will return to V8 engines from 2030 in a move FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has described as "an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA" of the sport. Earlier this week, Ben Sulayem teased the possibility of V8 engines ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, live on Sky Sports F1 , with the sound of a screaming F1 car with a caption: "You spoke, we listened. V8s coming soon." On Friday, the FIA announced a technical framework had been unanimously agreed between the FIA, Formula One Management (FOM), the teams and Formula 1 power unit manufacturers to move to a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 power unit. The 35-year-old centre-back, who has won two Premier League titles and the Champions League during his time at Liverpool, is out of contract in the summer. Anderson is co-owner of Napoli Knights, with the 44-year-old's appearance his first since being released by boyhood club Lancashire at the end of the season. metadata.summary: Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes "standout candidate" Andy Murray will one day take the role he is vacating after more than 16 years.
metadata.content: Andy Murray: Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes Scot will one day take the role | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Andy Murray: Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes Scot will one day take the role Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes Andy Murray will one day take the role he is vacating; the Scot is not currently interested in taking over due to other commitments; You can watch the ATP Finals in Turin this week on Sky Sports Tennis Friday 20 November 2026 17:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Murray backs his brother Andy or Greg Rusedski to be the next Team GB Davis Cup captain after Leon Smith stepped down from the role after 17 years Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes "standout candidate" Andy Murray will one day take the role he is vacating after more than 16 years. Smith took over from John Lloyd in 2010 following a humiliating loss to Lithuania that left Britain facing relegation to the bottom level of the historic competition. Harnessing the talents and commitment of Murray, who he coached as a junior, Smith led Britain back to the top tier and, only five years later, to a first title since 1936 when they defeated Belgium in 2015.
